doc.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014

title: Rising costs and stagnant jazz pay
summary: Harper cites train fares and the Holland Tunnel toll, Jimmy Heath on unchanged pay, and club cover charges.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You know I think the last time I went to a club in New York, I think it was the Iridium. And Ron Carter had a group. It was very good but it was not his group, it was who can I get. But it cost me, this was probably ten years ago, it cost me I think almost $70, by the time I paid the cover and had a couple of drinks. And I’m wondering about two things. Like how does that kind of thing sustain itself, if we’re worried about our audience; and also what are those musicians getting paid?

Well it depends and that’s what I’m saying, that’s one of the difficult things now for jazz. And it’s not just jazz, it’s life period. Everything is so expensive. And who’s to be blamed? I’m not sure. I mean we all know somebody’s walking away with a bigger cut of the pie, you know, than it needs to be, where it makes it unfair. But it’s caused everything to go up to the point where the little people are getting squeezed out and screaming or complaining. Even these talks about minimum wage. I mean on the one hand the people are talking about it’s not enough, I can understand that. Because of the cost of living. I always tell my kids, I mean when I first came to New York, and I’ve been living over in Jersey for a long time, to get on the Path train, which was just to go from New Jersey to New York, was under a dollar. You know what I mean? It was under a dollar. I think it was maybe like 50 cents or something, just to go — because like the whole ride to go from Jersey to New York is like 20 minutes. So it was under a dollar. Now? It just went up I think a couple of days ago, so now it’s $2.75 for one trip. You know what I mean? But over the years it’s gone up. I think when I first got to New York, to drive and go through the Holland Tunnel was like $2. Whatever. It was under $5. I mean to go through the Holland Tunnel now, any time I’ve got to go to work that means every night, to go through that tunnel I have to spend — it costs right now, it’s $13. You know what I mean? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

And now they’re saying that every year all of these are going up a certain amount of money. So I was just telling my kids the other day, so that means look, in another ten years to go from New Jersey to New York by the train is going to be almost a $5 ride. So if you just want to go hang out you’re looking at at least $10 just to take the train. Now driving-wise in ten years it may be almost $20 just for the toll. Everything is just —
You know but this occurs to me, and it seems like one of the things that keeps getting cheaper and cheaper to the point of being ridiculous is buying music.

Well that’s ‘cause musicians aren’t making any money. I was just talking to Jimmy Heath the other day and you know we were laughing and talking about the cost of things. And I said yeah everything is going up but what — jazz musicians have been making the same amount of money since I came along. I mean I’m talking to Jimmy Heath who is like 88 or something. And I said I’ve been here at least 30 years myself. The pay hasn’t changed. I mean the garbage man pay has gone up. You know what I mean? But most of the jazz musicians are still making the same amount of money. So that’s what I mean, I have to tell a lot of the young guys now, you really have to think about this. Because some of the gigs I used to take, let’s say if I was going into New York and I had somebody call me up for a gig. Okay so if it was a hundred dollar gig, you know sometimes I have to think about it. Because you’ve got already, just off the bat, you put gas in the car, you’ve spent $13 for the tunnel, if you’ve got to put your car in the garage, you know you’ve already spent half your money before you do the gig.

So in answer to what you were saying, sometimes that’s why those cover charges now are so high. Because it’s hard for a jazz club even to sustain itself a lot of times because those rents now, rents for everybody, leases, it’s terrible. What they’re asking for is just like — I never thought it was going to get to be this expensive.
